memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses answered, "As soon as I leave you, I will pray to the Lord, and tomorrow the flies will leave Pharaoh and his officials and his people. Only let Pharaoh be sure that he does not act deceitfully again by not letting the people go to offer sacrifices to the Lord."" - Exodus 8:29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses agrees to pray, and then adds a firm warning: do not act deceitfully again.

Notice that Moses is kind and honest at the same time. He does not withhold the prayer to punish Pharaoh, and he does not pretend the previous betrayal never happened. He serves the man while naming the truth.

That is a rare combination. We usually swing to one extreme or the other — either we become bitter and withhold kindness, or we become so eager to keep peace that we never name what is wrong. Paul described the healthy alternative as speaking the truth in love (Eph 4:15).

The word deceitfully is the key one. Pharaoh had promised, received relief, and broken his word. He was treating God as someone who could be handled.

We should search ourselves here. Do we ever bargain with God in trouble and quietly forget the terms afterwards? God is not deceived, and He is not mocked (Gal 6:7).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can I be kind to someone and still tell them the truth?
2. Have I made promises to God that I have quietly walked away from?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make me truthful and kind together. Forgive me for promises I have broken with You. Amen.
